title: Algebraic-space quotient of a free flat group-space action
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $B,Z$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ with a morphism $Z\to B$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. A group algebraic space $G$ over $B$ means an algebraic space $G\to B$ whose functor on $B$-schemes is a sheaf of groups, with multiplication, identity and inverse given by morphisms over $B$. Let $a:G\times_B Z\to Z$ be a left action over $B$: on every test scheme its maps satisfy $1z=z$ and $(gh)z=g(hz)$, naturally under pullback. Assume the action is free on every test scheme, meaning $gz=z$ implies $g=1$, and assume $G\to B$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Form the fppf sheafification $F=Z/G$ of the orbit presheaf on $S$-schemes [def-pc-fppf-site, def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Then $F$ is an algebraic space, and $q:Z\to F$ is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation. Moreover $q$ has fppf local sections on every scheme test $T\to F$, and the morphism $G\times_B Z\to Z\times_F Z$, $(g,z)\mapsto(gz,z)$, is an isomorphism of fppf sheaves. Surjectivity means surjectivity on field-valued point classes [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]; all fibre products are sheaf fibre products.

proof.text: We use algebraic spaces as discrete fppf stacks: unique gluing of sections gives descent of objects and arrows. Their diagonals are representable by schemes by [def-trf-algebraic-space]; a scheme is an algebraic space by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Their etale scheme charts are representable smooth surjections by [lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-representable-smooth-calculus]. Thus they satisfy [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and maps between them are representable by algebraic spaces by the same calculus. We can consequently apply [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] to algebraic-space maps: flatness and local finite presentation are stable under arbitrary base change and composition, and etale maps have both properties. The chart interpretation agrees with the assumed chartwise flatness and local finite presentation of $G\to B$: for charts $V\to B$ and $W\to G\times_BV$, [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test] tests flatness and local finite presentation on $W\to V$, independently of the charts. The calculus instead tests a property after every scheme base change $T\to B$. These agree: etale scheme charts are surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation, so the algebraic-space source-and-target clause of [lem-sfb-representable-fppf-etale-open-descent], applied to $V\to B$ and $W\to G\times_BV$, says that $G\to B$ has the property in the calculus sense if and only if $W\to V$ has it. Taking identity target charts gives the same interpretation for maps to schemes.

source.place: Tag 06PH (lemma-quotient-free-action), base-change conventions; spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 03MO and 03XR.

proof.text: Let $P(T)$ be the set of orbits in $Z(T)$, where two sections can be related only if their maps to $B$ agree, and then by an element of the corresponding group $G(T)$. The map $P\to B$ is well defined because the action is over $B$. Since $B$ is an fppf sheaf, the universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] extends it uniquely to $F\to B$ with composite $Z\to B$ the given map. Form $R=G\times_BZ$, an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], with $s(g,z)=z$ and $t(g,z)=gz$. Its identity, inverse and composition are $(1,z)$, $(g^{-1},gz)$ and $(h,gz)\circ(g,z)=(hg,z)$. The action axioms give the groupoid laws. If $gz=hz$, then $(h^{-1}g)z=z$, so freeness gives $g=h$. Thus $(t,s)$ is injective on all test-scheme sections and identifies $R$ with an equivalence relation. The orbit presheaf and hence its sheafification are exactly $P$ and $F$.

The natural map $R\to Z\times_FZ$, $(g,z)\mapsto(gz,z)$, is an isomorphism of sheaves. Indeed, for $(x,y)$ over $T$ with $q(x)=q(y)$, [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] applied to their orbit classes gives an fppf covering $T_i\to T$ on which $x_i=g_i y_i$ for some $g_i$. Their maps to $B$ agree globally, since $F\to B$ was constructed in step 2. On every overlap $g_i=g_j$ by freeness. The fppf sheaf property of $G$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] glues them uniquely to $g$, with $x=gy$ by the sheaf property of $Z$. Uniqueness also gives compatibility with pullback. This constructs a natural inverse. Furthermore, for every $f\in F(T)$, the local-section clause of the same sheafification lemma gives an fppf covering $T_i\to T$ and orbit classes represented by $z_i\in Z(T_i)$ with $q(z_i)=f|_{T_i}$. Thus $q$ already has fppf local sections on every scheme test.

For $f\in F(T)$ put $E=h_T\times_FZ$, a sheaf. Choose the covering and lifts $z_i$ of step 3. The kernel-pair isomorphism identifies $E\times_TT_i$ with $T_i\times_{z_i,Z,s}R$: a point is $(u,x)$ with $q(x)=q(z_i(u))$, uniquely $(u,g)$ with $x=gz_i(u)$. This is also $T_i\times_BG$, hence an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Choose etale scheme charts of these local algebraic spaces in the working universe. The covering index and charts lie in that universe [def-weil-size-convention], and their scheme coproduct exists by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] and belongs to the ambient big site. Therefore all hypotheses, including the chart-size condition, of [lem-sfb-fppf-local-algebraic-space] hold. It follows that $E$ is an algebraic space over $T$, before any assertion of algebraicity of $F$.

source.place: Tag 04SK (lemma-locally-algebraic-space); Tag 06PH, local calculation underlying Tag 06PG.

proof.text: Each $E\times_TT_i\simeq T_i\times_BG\to T_i$ is flat and locally of finite presentation by step 1 and the hypothesis on $G\to B$. It has a section $u\mapsto(u,1)$, so it is surjective. Let $T'=\coprod_iT_i$, which exists by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] in [def-weil-size-convention]. The maps $T_i\to T$ are flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-pc-fppf-site]; the open-source locality of [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] gives these properties for $T'\to T$. It is surjective because the family covers. Similarly $E\times_TT'\to T'$ has both properties, since on the disjoint open pieces it is the displayed projection. Apply the algebraic-space clause of [lem-sfb-representable-fppf-etale-open-descent] to $E\to T$ with the single cover $T'\to T$. Thus $E\to T$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. It is surjective on field-valued point classes: a field point of $T$ lifts to a point of some covering $T_i$ after field extension, and the displayed section then lifts it to $E$. No quasi-compactness of the covering is required.

Apply [lem-sfb-fppf-space-atlas-bootstrap] to the fppf sheaf $F$ and $q:Z\to F$. The source $Z$ is an algebraic space by hypothesis. For every $T$ and $f\in F(T)$, step 4 gives the required algebraic space $E$, and step 5 gives surjectivity, flatness and local finite presentation of its projection. Thus $F$ is an algebraic space. The same projections show that $q$ is flat and locally of finite presentation on charts; field-point surjectivity follows from the local lifts of step 3. Step 3 also gives all requested local sections and the exact isomorphism $G\times_BZ\simeq Z\times_FZ$ with formula $(g,z)\mapsto(gz,z)$. These prove every clause.
